quest.title: Sincerity's Facade
quest.description: The truth is revealed. Dehya's father has long passed. Still, his comrades in arms seek to avenge him. Before judgment falls, Dehya decides to lend them her aid.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x700, Primogem x60, Mora x47175, Guide to Praxis x5, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

talks.objective: Go to the hiding place of Deshret's Relics

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Paimon didn't expect it to look like this on the inside...

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: They should all be holed up in here. Dunno how many people they've got left, though.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Who cares? We'll round up all of 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Tikriti
dialogues.text: Still, we should be careful. Even if they've only got one shot left, it could still take us out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've fought through many situations like this before.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah, we'll know what they're really capable of once we've landed some hits on 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Deshret's Relics may have been a force to be reckoned with before, but their name means nothing now.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Yeah, they don't stand a chance with you here. I'll take the lead, I've been here once before.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: This way, follow me! We're almost there!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, they went charging ahead without checking for any traps!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey! You guys okay?

dialogues.speaker: Bashar
dialogues.text: It seems like we just got trapped in here... don't think we triggered anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Watch out, the enemy's coming from ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Tikriti
dialogues.text: Well, now that things have come to this, seems we'll have to fight our way through.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Don't worry about us, we knew something like this could happen! Go and take a look around — there could still be another way through!

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Let's go, we can't let the boss down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's check if there's another way! The sooner we can make it through to help them, the better!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I think I see a way through over there, but it's being blocked by something. Let's try our luck with that mechanism.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: I wasn't expecting anyone to make it through from the other side.

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: But as a desert-dweller, I suppose we should be used to our folks defying all expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't waste your breath. You have nowhere to run.

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: Run? Heh, had I wanted to run, I would have fled a thousand times already.

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: I witnessed the golden age of Deshret's Relics. Even if I could leave this place behind, all that awaits me now are endless days of humiliation and ruin.

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: Even now, my brothers and I still believe in one thing.

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: "The greatest should never live to remember their fall."

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmph... so you want to go out in a blaze of glory.

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: Let us draw our weapons. We will show them the true power King Deshret bestowed upon his followers.

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: They are but two, while we hold within ourselves the entirety of the Relics' glory.

talks.objective: Fight back against the remaining members of Deshret's Relics
Talk to Dehya about how to respond

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The commander has finally fallen.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But they're still coming at us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This place is like a gladiator's ring... They just keep coming, no matter how many we beat!

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: Yes, keep fighting! There's no need to fear, and no need to back down. This is our last stand!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: When the next wave comes, try to draw away their attacks.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm going to see if I can take out that high platform.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Get out of my way!

dialogues.speaker: Bashar
dialogues.text: Come and face me, Mishal!

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: Ah, so they've broken through the front as well...

dialogues.speaker: Scared Mercenary
dialogues.text: Apologies, Mishal, they just — they fight like absolute mad men! No matter how much we throw at them, they just keep coming for more!

dialogues.speaker: Scared Mercenary
dialogues.text: ARGH!

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: So, it would seem like this is the end.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Time to pay for everything you've done, Mishal.

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: Heh, you think I would give you that opportunity?

dialogues.speaker: Mishal
dialogues.text: I will be buried in the sand alongside all the rest of our fading glory.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Hey, wait!

dialogues.speaker: Bashar
dialogues.text: We were too late...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...It's over, there's no more need to fight.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But if you're still going to cling onto your so-called mercenaries' pride, then I'll give you all a good beating as well.

dialogues.speaker: Tikriti
dialogues.text: Hey, Dehya! I've found the mechanism. I'll get you all back up here right away!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: Who are you filthy rats, and why are you always pestering us?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hah, you call yourself a member of the infamous Deshret's Relics, and you still can't even tell who's made it all the way to your headquarters?

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: Who knows what intent a bunch of rats may have? We try to catch a couple, and you all just show up on the other side instead. How are we supposed to figure out what you're after?

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Hey, have you ever heard of a man by the name of Kusayla?

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: Wh—Why would I know? It's not like I'm in charge or anything!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: This is your last chance to talk.

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: H—Hey, I said I don't know anything! I'm just an average member here. I'm telling the truth!

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: If you're here to find someone, why don't you look through the records yourselves? Who can remember every name and face with so many people coming in and out every day?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The irony.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: His life became a light for so many, yet to others, it wasn't even worth remembering.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Where's the records room? Answer me.

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: It's right over there, all the files are in there! You can go through them as much as you want, it's not like any of them still matter anyway!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I mean the old records room.

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: Th—The old records room? You mean... the one that got burned down?

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: Kusayla! Ah yeah, I remember him now. The guy who could hardly walk!

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Watch your mouth! That's our boss you're talking about!

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: He was definitely faking it! We all let down our guard as soon as we saw him come hobbling in...

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: But in the short time it supposedly took him to take a dump, he'd already gotten away, and started a fire in the records room...

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: He couldn't have possibly outrun us if he wasn't a fraud!

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: ...And after that, Deshret's Relics fell into complete disarray.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Stop wasting our time. Every one of us here is perfectly aware of what he had done.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Tell me. Where is the old records room?

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: It's just over there, go see it for yourself if it means that much to you!

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: There's nothing left in there but ashes. No human could ever survive that kind of inferno.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Bashar, Tikriti, let's go. We'll leave the others here to guard these guys.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Spare them no mercy if they try anything.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So this was his final destination.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: How did he do it...? Getting past all the guards with a limp, and sneaking in here to start a fire...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If he was nimble enough to do that, then he must've been able to get out of here after starting the fire, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I know it's just wishful thinking. Let's look around. Maybe we can find something that's been left behind.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone searches around the room...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Is this a cane? It must be the one that Dehya's father used...

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Kusayla...

dialogues.speaker: Bashar
dialogues.text: Thanks for everything, boss.

dialogues.speaker: Tikriti
dialogues.text: We're fortunate to somehow find that cane after that fire.

dialogues.speaker: Idrisi
dialogues.text: Let's split up and look around some more. What if something else has been left behind?

dialogues.speaker: Tikriti
dialogues.text: But what else could survive a fire like that?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wh—What's this?

choices.text: We got you some snacks and drinks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't you remember? You asked Paimon what she would do if she were to wake up tomorrow with loads of money!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon said that she would get boatloads of tasty snacks! You looked super confused at the time, but said it was an adorable thing to say!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: These opportunities don't come by often, so today, Paimon's gonna treat you to a special crash course on Paimon's life philosophy!

choices.text: She rarely spends her allowance on other people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, c'mon! Paimon's not that stingy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, the point is that you should eat to your heart's content! You'll feel better for sure once you've gotten something in your tummy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dunyarzad will also be here shortly! She's already heard that we're back.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Aw, thanks, you two. Honestly, this is very unlike me. I just had a lot on my mind on our way back, so I didn't know what to say...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: My chest was filled with all kinds of intense emotions. They just shook me even more than all the feelings we've shared during our previous adventures.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But when everything came to an end, those emotions also vanished without a trace, and I was left feeling more empty than ever before.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It was as if... I'd lost the thing that was most important to me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Everything just happened so fast.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, you're right. To many mercenaries, Mora is the most important thing in the world. But perhaps to us, it's the most worthless thing of all.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Idrisi and the others all used to say that they would quit if there was no Mora to be had. But when it came to avenging my father, there was no Mora to be made anywhere.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: My reality shattered when I found out that the father who always told me hero stories was in fact a bad guy, but look at me now... am I any different?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Despite all my promises about never forgiving him, and never trying to understand him, I still went to such lengths to find out the truth, and nearly even shed tears for his sake...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: We're hypocrites, all of us.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You should never question your true feelings, though.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah, you're right. It's just a pity that we often only recognize our true feelings after it's already too late.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: You're back! Are all of you alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, there she is!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Yeah... Many people from the Corps of Thirty came over, and I just wrapped up everything with my dad. All I can do now is wait for their verdict...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Huh? Dehya, you're looking quite down again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon will explain! A lot happened while we were gone...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Once Paimon finishes telling the story, Dunyarzad begins to cry. It takes some time for her to compose herself.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I'm sorry, I really should have controlled my emotions better, I just... I just...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It's alright, my lady. You were hurt by all of this as well. Truth be told, I'm starting to feel a little guilty, watching you cry like this...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: But Dehya, your pain must be even worse. You shouldn't need to comfort me.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hey, don't worry about me. If anything, this whole thing has finally shown me the difference between illusion and reality.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: My father probably thought that people could settle into new lives as long as they moved to a new environment.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That thought has even crossed my mind a few times. It's like saying, "what's wrong with adapting to a new life?"

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: However, there was always something deep within my mind that refused to accept it. This impulse brought me great turmoil, and even made me feel ashamed for turning my back on your father's kindness...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: But now that I consider it again, it all makes sense. The desert sands are a part of who I am, and I will never be able to lead a peaceful existence.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I understand how you feel.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That doesn't mean I won't be making any changes to my life, though. As an example, I'm now thinking about taking on some small, odd jobs.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It's just like Idrisi said... I also want to catch up to my father, and become a character in his play.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Even if the ending of the story may be childish and ridiculous, it won't really matter...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Isn't that neat though? You'll be a whole new kind of mercenary, one that's not out for Mora!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Why don't we go for a change of scenery once we finish eating? What about stopping by the Grand Bazaar again?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Right, you said you wanted to get a rug for your family...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll come along, too!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's always more fun when everyone's together.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Haha, I can't thank you enough for taking care of me this entire time.

choices.text: It's really my treat, but you get the point.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, this way you get something from the both of us for the price of one!

talks.objective: Go to the Grand Bazaar to clear your head

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: This rug here is quite something... the craftsmanship is exquisite, and the fabric is also of high quality.

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: Ah, here you are. Finally, I found you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, a—aren't you that mercenary who bit his tongue? You can still talk?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Are you here to take revenge on us?

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: Hah, what are you talking about? Do I look like I could take you all in a fight? I just came here to give you something. I'll be on my way to give myself up to the Corps after this.

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: Once I woke up, I hurried to Dakan Al-Ahmar's camp, hoping to alert them to your presence.

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: But when I got there, I found no one except the members who were still too injured to move.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah, so you probably got there after us...

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: Yeah, they told me that they had exacted their revenge, and everyone had turned themselves in to the authorities. Even that last camp was not going to last for much longer.

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: I had joined the cause to repay an old favor from Kusayla. Now that everyone's already turned themselves in, I might as well do the same.

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: One of the injured members gave this box to me, and told me that it contained some of the old man's last possessions.

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: Everything left in the camp will get confiscated, so I figured I should get this to you before the Corps could get their hands on it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Sattar
dialogues.text: No worries. We are all just living our own truths. There's no need to comment or judge anyone for it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this box contains everything that Dehya's father left behind... Huh, it feels lighter than expected.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Well, back in the day, the first thing he did with any Mora was spend it on things like drinks and meat.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But let's see what's inside...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wh—What's this? It's just a bunch of junk! ...Ugh, it kinda stinks...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Uhh... perhaps it's just been left unopened for too long?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: A handwritten copy of a storybook... The paper's already yellowed, and it looks like it's about to fall apart...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It was against the Akademiya's rules to possess books for personal use. If he was going to break that rule, he could have at least copied something useful...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That probably means this was really important to him.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ah, and here are a few bags of children's snacks... the packaging's completely deteriorated. Maybe that's where the smell was coming from.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Did he get those for you?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yeah, but here's the thing though... Even when I was a child, I was never a fan of these kinds of snacks. He'd always say that he got them for me, but in the end, he always ate more than I ever did...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Who even leaves snacks in a box like this, anyway? Isn't that just common sense...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Forget it, let me see what else is here...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: A razor, some buttons, some round iron tiles, a wooden toy puppet...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: A wool scarf, which from the looks of it probably belonged to a woman, and a hair clip... why are these things here?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I—I'm suddenly feeling a little scared...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, my lady, but this is just the kind of man he was. He probably saw this box as some kind of personal trash heap, and dumped any and everything in here...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: One, no, two empty liquor bottles... Ugh, tell me you guys, are these the kinds of things that a normal person would leave behind?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? There's something in the bottle!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Oh, you're right...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Alright, I got it out. It seems to be a piece of paper with some writing on it. The bottom part's all damaged from moisture, though... let's hope the writing didn't smudge.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: "I was suddenly seized with an urge to write a letter after finishing this bottle. I just folded it up and left it in the bottle, though. If I end up forgetting about it, it won't really matter."

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: "To Dehya..." It's a letter for me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You don't need to read it out loud.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It's alright, I'll just read it out. If he went to the trouble of writing a letter, there must have been some important things that he wanted to say... or at least, record down.

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "My condition's becoming worse and worse. Can't even walk without a cane anymore, much less go out and have fun. Guess I don't have many days left."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "If you're reading this letter, then I suppose I'm already long gone."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "You were adorable as a baby. Everyone loved you, and regardless of whether you were crying or laughing, everyone enjoyed having you in the group."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "But once you grew a bit older, you were no longer nearly as happy or cute. It's probably the guys' fault..."

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hah, can you believe this guy? He can point the finger at himself.

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "Anyway, back to the point... To summarize, I'm writing this so you would know not to feel sad for me even if you end up finding out the truth."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "The reason being that... Heh, I was never your father to begin with."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what!?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Surely... he must be joking, right?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I... I don't know...

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "Hah, I was quite formidable when I was young! And a hundred times cooler than some so-called 'Flame-Mane,' hahaha."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "It really felt like the whole world was under my feet. With just a teeny tiny bit of effort, I felt I could rule over the entire desert."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "But as fate would have it, I went out into the desert for a drink one day, and discovered a baby in the sands. It was you."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "You were just lying there, small and helpless. You were so tiny that if the wind blew for just a little while longer, you would have been buried forever."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "But your cries were so loud, they made my head hurt. Now that I think of it, you really were a bundle of energy."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... sounds like he's serious.

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "I told Idrisi and the others that I had slipped up with a woman while out and about. None of them even doubted me."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "I'm sorry that I had to lie to them for so long, but I really had no other choice."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "I was their most esteemed leader, after all. It's not like I could just tell them that I suddenly wanted to play at being a father..."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "Haha, at this rate, I'll puke up all the liquor I just drank from this bottle."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "Anyway, Dehya..."

response.speaker: Kusayla's Letter
response.text: "You possess the kind of freedom and kindness that we could only dream of. As for how you should live your life... that'll be up to you to decide."

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: That's... the end of the letter.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...In the end, he was still thinking of me as a little child.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But isn't that also a good thing?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I suppose, or I would have suffocated under the sand a long time ago.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: He was a good father to you. The fact that he wasn't a blood relative doesn't change that.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Yeah. It's just a pity that we had to learn the truth of everything like this.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Do you already have some ideas about the decision that he wanted you to make?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I do. If he first found me alone in the sands, then I want to try my hand at finding the person who abandoned me.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I just have one wish, to tell them a story...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...That there once existed a childish and foolish jerk with a heart of gold.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: And that only under his care was I able to grow and mature into the person I am today.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you end up finding any leads, can you share them with us? We go on adventures all the time. Maybe we'll be able to find some information for you.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Sure, I appreciate it. I wasn't expecting you to be so enthusiastic.

choices.text: I also don't want to see his efforts go to waste.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I'll help too!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Thank you, all of you. Thank you so much.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: My life has certainly had its twists and turns, but I've always considered myself lucky.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Because no matter where I've gone, I've always been surrounded by incredible kindness.

choices.text: I don't want you to stop going forward.

dialogues.speaker: Mirza
dialogues.text: Ugh, what a bummer. I just had to get injured now, right before the final fight...

dialogues.speaker: Mirza
dialogues.text: Be sure to punch one of 'em for me.

dialogues.speaker: Ayyoub
dialogues.text: I guess it all comes down to this...

dialogues.speaker: Shakhbout
dialogues.text: I've already told you everything I know, can't you just leave me alone?

dialogues.speaker: Hamzah
dialogues.text: Wave one, charge! Eliminate them!

dialogues.speaker: Hamzah
dialogues.text: King Deshret will not abandon any one of his followers!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
The whole story was shared with the Corps of Thirty, which finally joined the investigation in the name of restoring order.
The members of Deshret's Relics were brought to justice, and the members of Dakan Al-Ahmar turned themselves in to the authorities.
The cane that once belonged to Kusayla was given to Dehya as a part of her inheritance.
Dehya was completely silent on the way back to Sumeru City.
